findings.title: clara._prepayment_plan_core_wake duplicates ~25 lines of clara._obo_plan_core's plan-write tail verbatim, the exact two-copies risk this lane's own #915 report argued against
findings.evidence: packages/db/migrations/0315_prepayment_wake_reroute.sql:237-276 (`_prepayment_plan_core_wake`, from `if p_purpose is null or btrim(p_purpose) = ''` through the closing `return jsonb_build_object('plan_id', ...)`) is line-for-line the same sequence as packages/db/migrations/0308_deferred_revenue_recognition.sql:611-676 (`_obo_plan_core`'s tail): the purpose-blank check, `clara._assert_plan_schedule(...)`, `clara._assert_journal_basis`, `_journal_basis_digest`, `pg_advisory_xact_lock(203005004, hashtext(p_client::text))`, the two `insert into clara.accounting_plans` / `clara.accounting_plan_revisions` statements with identical column lists, `clara._plan_overlap_warning`, the `clara._plan_due_events` jsonb_agg, the `clara._audit(...)` call with the same verb, and the same `return jsonb_build_object('plan_id', 'revision_id', 'revision', 'status', 'kind', 'next_occurrences', 'overlap_warning')` shape. Only the ~10-line authority-resolution preamble differs (an `_authority_ref_refusal` call in `_obo_plan_core` vs. a shape check on `{kind:'agent_wake', wake_kind, task_id}` in `_prepayment_plan_core_wake`) and a few local variable names (`p_author`/`p_actor`, `p_kind` literal vs argument).
findings.why_it_matters: This is exactly the risk #915's own report (docs/plan/active/riders-2026-09-20/reports/wave4-lane04-ticket915.md, 'why it departs from 0222's precedent') names and extracts against for the SCHEDULE body: 'Two copies make [AC4's promise] a promise; one body makes it a fact,' citing the accrual lane's own measured drift (`_accrual_plan_core` vs `create_accounting_plan`) as the cautionary example. #1036's migration header repeats the same argument ('So this file does to the PLAN STEP what #915 did to the SCHEDULE BODY: ONE body...') but does not actually apply it: the write tail below the authority check is now duplicated in a THIRD place instead of extracted into one shared inner function called by both `_obo_plan_core` and `_prepayment_plan_core_wake` after each resolves authority its own way. A later change to the audit payload shape, the overlap-warning call, or the due-events preview window has two call sites to update, and a maintainer who edits one (as `_accrual_plan_core` already demonstrates happened for the accrual family) can silently leave the other stale.
findings.required_fix: Extract the shared tail (advisory lock through the return shape) into one function, e.g. `clara._plan_write_core(p_kind, p_firm, p_client, p_actor, p_purpose, p_authority_kind, p_authority_ref, p_via, p_frequency, p_day_rule, p_day_of_month, p_timezone, p_effective_from, p_effective_to, p_basis)`, and have `_obo_plan_core` and `_prepayment_plan_core_wake` each resolve/validate authority in their own way and then delegate to it -- the same pattern #915 used to collapse the human and OBO schedule bodies into `_prepayment_schedule_core`. This is a forward-looking refactor for the next migration to take, since 0315 is already applied on this lane's database (never edit an applied migration); worth a follow-up ticket rather than a same-migration fix.

findings.title: The whole #941 web feature (3 pages, 5 components, 2 lib modules, a 471-line render-states test file) landed in one commit, and by the report's own account was inherited mid-flight rather than built in this session's own red-green cycles
findings.evidence: `git log --oneline --stat cd2925391..HEAD -- apps/web/components/deferred-revenue apps/web/lib/deferred-revenue apps/web/app` shows commit `adde3a6d9` alone adding 2,550 insertions across 11 files (3 route pages, `deferred-revenue-attention.tsx`, `deferred-revenue-detail.tsx`, `deferred-revenue-form.tsx`, `deferred-revenue-list.tsx`, `deferred-revenue-statement.tsx`, `deferred-revenue-render-states.test.tsx`, `lib/deferred-revenue/api.ts`, `lib/deferred-revenue/schedule.ts`) in a single commit. The ticket report (docs/plan/active/riders-2026-09-20/reports/wave4-lane04-ticket941.md, 'A note on what I inherited') states this tree was already present, UNCOMMITTED, on the branch when this session started, and that 'Everything from adde3a6d9 on is mine, including the repairs to what I inherited.'
findings.why_it_matters: WORK-ORDER.md rule 4 requires vertical slices -- 'one test → see it red for the right reason → the minimal code that turns it green' -- committed 'per green slice or per small group of slices,' specifically to avoid a whole feature landing as one undifferentiated block. Because this code predates the reviewing/authoring session, the git history cannot show whether it was actually built test-first in slices or written as a batch and tested afterward; the report is transparent about this and supplies vacuity controls (6bec1e822, 3e68d8ace) proving the cells it added on top actually bite against the inherited code, which mitigates but does not fully answer the process question for the inherited 2,550-line commit itself.
findings.required_fix: No code change needed. Worth a note to the orchestrator/integrator that #941's web layer's TDD provenance before this session picked it up is unverifiable from history alone, so if that layer is audited for test quality later, treat `deferred-revenue-render-states.test.tsx`'s cells authored before `adde3a6d9` as unverified-vertical-slice rather than confirmed-compliant.
